question: Is the listener-described vibration necessarily a programmed lead vibrato, and did a static lead patch substitution capture the reference sound?
scope: Bounded original-source full/lead/backing diagnostics from initialization through35s; no source edits, patch intervention or perceptual verdict.

settings.sidModel: MOS6581 explicitly assumed; source header unknown
settings.ROMs: same pinned C64 ROM files as songs/pink-panther/basic-reference.json
settings.voiceMask: libsidplayfp control-mask diagnostic, not output-only muting

independenceBasis: Decoded source uses pulse only without ring/sync, filter routing, SID reads, or volume digi during this passage; source snapshots are not internal mute state or exact bus timestamps.

method.implementation: NumPy 2.4.6 and scipy.signal using existing .tools/songbench-venv; no model inference
method.filter: Fourth-order Butterworth plus/minus12Hz around expected lead frequency, zero-phase sosfiltfilt on complete35s PCM; analytic Hilbert phase/envelope then selected settled body windows
method.pitchEstimate: Least-squares analytic phase slope;100ms independent subwindow slopes reported without FFT-bin quantization
method.amplitudeCV: Standard deviation/mean of analytic narrowband amplitude; this measures local band motion, not perceived vibrato or loudness. Main backing estimates near absent lead harmonics are intentionally omitted.

structuralFindings: Complete decoded BASIC source has no continuing pitch, pulse-width, waveform or filter modulation loop; wait loop only checks TI. Negative high-byte fields selectively reattack, positive fields retune under a high gate.
BASIC writes frequency high then low with snapshot-visible intermediate pitches at transitions; no causal audibility or exact duration claim follows from these snapshots.
Intro0.65-15s combines all three identical bright narrow-pulse patches and repeatedly changes bass beneath held upper voices; a lead-only patch substitution does not preserve this texture.

Main-theme selected17.45-31.45s opens D#3/E3 in both BASIC source and our native score; there is no octave disparity in these compared opening pickups. Later BASIC repetition moves up an octave, outside this diagnostic.

Our transfer retains a different source arrangement, triangle support, and native gate/TEST scheduling. Exact ADSR/waveform/width fields do not establish equivalent articulation, motion or ensemble balance.

conclusion.highConfidence: The sampled settled solo lead bodies have effectively stationary pitch; explicit periodic vibrato is absent from decoded source. The intro full mix contains measurable narrowband amplitude/phase movement while the corresponding solo body is stationary.
conclusion.causalInference: Near-coincident harmonics of bright pulse voices, changing accompaniment/envelopes, and selective rearticulation can contribute to perceived animation. Their relative perceptual contribution remains unsettled.
conclusion.notEstablished: The user's perceived vibration has not been localized by listening, nor has ensemble beating been proven to be its sole cause. No fresh candidate patch or claimed musical acceptance.

order: Original full mix raw17.45-31.45s at unity gain
Original lead-only control-mask diagnostic for identical raw17.45-31.45s at unity gain
audition.listeningQuestion: Does the vibration you mean remain in the second, isolated-lead half, or mostly disappear with the other two voices?

introNearHarmonicPredictions.scope: Three coincident pitch words in intro; not a score transcription. Rates below derive from source-word differences scaled by measured solo pitch.
introNearHarmonicPredictions.limit: Predicted harmonic beating rates do not alone establish perceptual vibration or its cause.

introAudition.purpose: Includes the intro held-note body with measured ensemble motion; main theme diagnostic remains separately available.
